key_insight: LLM tutors often overintervene—acting too early and too often—and this can improve immediate answers while weakening deeper learning.
engineering_relevance: For AI tutoring and copilots, intervention policy matters as much as correctness: systems should prefer timed hints over full solutions to preserve user reasoning and transfer.
method: Introduced Int-Bench, a simulation benchmark for teacher-style interventions during problem solving.
Compared LLM and human teachers across code debugging, mathematics, and brain teasers.
Evaluated when and how often assistants intervene, plus effects on immediate success and generalization.
evidence_signal: Across three simulated domains, the benchmark shows LLMs intervene more frequently and earlier than humans, and they more often give complete solutions instead of targeted hints.
watch_item: Simulation-based results may not fully capture real learner behavior, so deployment should validate intervention policies with human users before optimization.
